call_points.text: EBITDA expected to stay under pressure for the next couple of quarters until global crises normalise.
Polymer capacity being built to take turnover from ₹1,000 Cr to about ₹2,000 Cr.
Disc brakes and switches start to matter only from FY28; disc brake production has started for one major Indian OEM.
M&A paused for a year to avoid stressing the balance sheet during the capex cycle and demerger.
Rupee at an all-time low against the dollar raises import costs for electronic child parts; management flags it could weaken further.
BMS is being exited; no further money will be invested as OEMs have decided to control it in-house.
ACFMS 30% growth outlook is at risk; FY26 achieved 30% growth but management is unsure of meeting it going forward.
P3L turnover doubling target in three years is on track and may even be exceeded.
FY27 capex planned at ₹680–700 Cr as the previous capex cycle ended and capacity utilisation reached a peak.
Polymer prices up 55%, aluminium up 62%, semiconductors up 35% and memory control devices up 28%, with freight also rising.
Cost pass-through to OEMs is evolving; management does not expect full recovery and expects some earnings softening.
Instrument cluster market share maintained by volume and increased by value; no dip seen for three years given confirmed LOIs.
About 75–80% of Tata cars come with Pricol clusters; the company is yet to enter Mahindra.
Segment mix: DICVS about 60% of revenue, ACFMS about 20% and P3L about 20%.
Dividend retained at 200% for FY26 to conserve cash amid capex and headwinds, after an interim Golden Jubilee dividend.
M&A is being evaluated cautiously; active negotiations and due diligence are in progress but no details were given.

guidance.statement: Exports targeted at 10% of revenue in coming years
P3L turnover to double in three years after takeover
Revenue target of ₹8,000 Cr for Calendar Year 2030 / FY31, from primarily organic and some inorganic growth
Polymer capacity to support about ₹2,000 Cr turnover from current ₹1,000 Cr
DICVS to grow at least 5% above market; ACFMS 10% above market

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Automobile and Auto Components > Auto Components > Auto Components & Equipments

operating_notes.text: P3L FY26 revenue was ₹924 Cr with a 9.24% EBITDA margin; about ₹65 Cr of foaming business transferred back to TVS will not continue.
Non-brake revenue in the ACFMS segment was about ₹750 Cr, or 96–97% of the segment's revenue.
About 75–80% of Tata cars come with Pricol clusters; the company is yet to enter Mahindra.
Polymer division Q1FY27 revenue was ₹249 Cr with 7.8% EBITDA margin.
Two-wheeler TFT cluster penetration is about 7-8% of production, expected to double in 2-3 years.
DIS market share: 30-35% in two-wheelers, about two-thirds in CVs, 8-9% in passenger vehicles.

timeline.summary: On its 15 May 2026 Q4FY26 call, Pricol reported FY26 revenue just shy of ₹4,000 Cr and guided ₹680–700 Cr of FY27 capex while flagging input-cost headwinds.

On 31 July 2026 Pricol's Q1FY27 call reported revenue of ₹1,083.58 Cr (+23.46% YoY), EBITDA of ₹123.69 Cr at 11.41% margin and PAT of ₹67.02 Cr (+34.34%), with management flagging cost headwinds and a ₹700 Cr capex cycle.

watchlist.response: Management said pass-through is evolving with a six-month lag, supplementary invoicing has been requested, and full recovery from OEMs is unlikely.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked how margin pressure from polymer, aluminium and semiconductor costs will be navigated over the next few quarters.

watchlist.response: Management declined to reaffirm the growth guidance, citing geopolitical uncertainty, and said it may miss the 30% ACFMS growth.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked whether the 13–15% growth guidance and 30% ACFMS growth outlook remain valid.

watchlist.response: Management declined, asking the analyst to contact the CFO for non-competitive data.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for segmental revenue split within the instrument cluster business by vehicle segment.
Demerger approvals from SEBI, ROC and NCLT

watchlist.response: Chairman said it is in line with industry seasonality (Q4 high, Q1 drops) and the company grew above market in each division.
watchlist.text: Sequential revenue was flattish despite strong YoY growth; analysts asked which businesses dragged.

watchlist.response: Chairman said the DIS business needs large investment and technology partners, and a combined entity struggled to attract the right investors.
watchlist.text: Analysts pressed on the demerger rationale, given the core cluster business becomes a single-product entity.

watchlist.response: Chairman said at minimum four quarters, hoped for 12 months, citing dependence on SEBI, ROC and NCLT; no firm date given.
watchlist.text: Analysts asked for a demerger timeline.

watchlist.response: Chairman said real revenues only kick in from FY28; no quarterly figure given.
